notices.title: External Cyclical Maintenance
notices.description:
The works include, but are not limited to, the provision of surveys and design services, consultation with customers including design development, and the scheduling and programming of all elements of the service. The works also encompass the installation, construction, repair, maintenance, renewal, reinstatement, replacement and/or improvement of structural components, roof coverings, fascias, bargeboards, soffits, rainwater goods, windows, external doors, fire safety measures, internal doors and frames, retrofit and energy efficiency measures, play areas, external paving, fencing and other environmental components, together with any additional works identified by the Client.
Window repairs or replacements undertaken as part of External Cyclical Maintenance Planned Schemes will generally involve a limited number of windows at an individual property. It is not anticipated that such schemes will require the replacement of a significant number of windows or the complete replacement of all windows within a property.
The works also include cyclical redecoration, comprising the redecoration of existing painted or decorated surfaces, including windows, doors, fascias, rainwater and sanitary pipework, walls, soffits to external elevations, and common areas including communal rooms. Cyclical redecoration may also extend to bin stores, garages, cycle sheds, fencing, railings, screens, gates and similar features located within boundaries, paths, drives, communal areas, staircases, access decks and balconies.
Cyclical redecoration shall be deemed to include the cleaning, where specified, of external surfaces of components and products such as windows, doors, soffits, fascias, cladding and other similar elements encountered during the works.
The works further include pre-decoration repairs, comprising the repair, maintenance, renewal, reinstatement or replacement of previously decorated elements and components where such works are required prior to cyclical redecoration. This includes the inspection, repair and adjustment of hinges, locking mechanisms, handles and security devices associated with UPVC windows and external or communal doors.
The works also include the identification, surveying, management, removal and disposal of asbestos-containing materials where these are discovered during the course of the works

notices.title: Design & Construction Framework
notices.description:
Northern Trains Limited is a Train Operating Company (TOC) that operates passenger rail services in the North of England. Northern Trains Limited is publishing this notice on behalf of itself and a number of 'Participating Authorities' including Train Operating Companies in Great Britain (see Section VI.3 below) to establish a framework for Design services, Design & Construction Works, and Construction Works to support the delivery of infrastructure, asset enhancement, refurbishment, renewal and construction projects across its network of stations, depots, train care centres and other operational property assets. 
The framework will enable Northern Trains Limited and the Participating Authorities to run mini-competitions for Design Services, Design & Construction Works, and Construction Works and directly award call-off contracts for their requirements among suppliers appointed to the framework.  
The Framework allows all Participating Authorities to use it, however, it has been developed primarily to serve the needs of the operators in the North of England, taking advantage of geographical synergies. Accordingly, its principal intended users are Northern Trains Limited (NTL), TransPennine Express (TPE) and London North Eastern Railway (LNER).
The objective of this procurement is to establish a multi-lot framework that will provide access to suitably qualified and experienced suppliers capable of delivering a range of design, construction and multidisciplinary project services. The framework comprises the following lots:
•	Lot 1: Internal Building Fit Outs
•	Lot 2: General Building and Civils
•	Lot 3: Minor Works and Reactive Projects
•	Lot 4: Multi-discipline Railway Solutions and Integrated Major Projects ≤ £1 million
•	Lot 5: Multi-discipline Railway Solutions and Integrated Major Projects > £1 million
•	Lot 6: Information and Security Systems Upgrades and Enhancements (SISS)
•	Lot 7: Accessible Stations Enhancements
The framework will support the delivery of projects ranging from feasibility and design development through to construction, installation, commissioning and handover. Services may include surveys, design activities, refurbishment works, asset renewals, building works, civil engineering, mechanical and electrical works, information and security systems, accessibility improvements and integrated multidisciplinary project delivery.
The scope of services will be delivered with the aim of meeting operational, performance and customer requirements whilst ensuring compliance with all applicable legislation, industry standards and railway-specific requirements. Suppliers will be expected to apply industry best practice, innovation and their technical expertise to achieve the following key objectives:
•	Deliver safe, high-quality and value-for-money design and construction solutions.
•	Support the enhancement, renewal and maintenance of NTL's operational estate and infrastructure assets.
•	Minimise disruption to passengers, train operations and depot activities during project delivery.
•	Ensure compliance with all relevant statutory, regulatory and rail industry requirements.
•	Promote sustainability, accessibility and social value outcomes across the framework.
•	Foster collaborative working and continuous improvement throughout the lifecycle of projects.
The nature of the arrangement is that Design Services, Design & Construction Works or Construction Works will be supplied under an NTL Framework Agreement and call offs will be using the full suite of JCT agreements, NEC4 agreements and other bespoke agreements, further detail can be found in tender documents. 
These requirements will be subject to competitive tendering among the members of the framework in accordance with the rules of the competitive flexible procedure as required by, and subject to, regulation sections 45 and 46 of the Procurement Act 2023. Specific contracts will be awarded according to those rules by the Northern Trains Limited or Participating Authorities in accordance with their specific requirements as set out in individual procurements under the framework. Suppliers appointed to the framework will be required to enter into a Framework Agreement setting out the terms on which the framework will operate including the standard terms and conditions that will be applicable to individual call-off contracts under the framework.
Northern Trains Limited is procuring on behalf of the Participating Authorities (as more particularly defined below) and will enter into the relevant framework agreement with the successful suppliers where such contracts are awarded. The Participating Authorities (as more particularly defined below) are permitted to use the framework via subsequent call-offs in accordance with section 1(3)(b) of the Procurement Act 2023. However, Northern Trains Limited is responsible for the conduct of the procurement throughout and all correspondence and communication from suppliers is to be solely with Northern Trains Limited.
Participating Authorities:
In addition to Northern Trains limited, the Participating Authorities who may call-off under this framework are: 
•	the Train Operating Companies
•	Network Rail Infrastructure Limited 
•	Any holders of a passenger licence or a station licence granted pursuant to section 8 of the Railways Act 1993 and/or a passenger licence granted pursuant to regulation 6 of the Railway (Licensing of Railway Undertakings) Regulations 2005 
Novation or Assignment
The framework agreement may be novated or assigned by Northern Trains Limited to Train Operating Companies, or to DFT Operator Limited (company number: 07141122) or any successor parent company to a Train Operating Company, following a corporate restructuring or similar circumstance. 
Other Information

notices.title: Boiler Room Upgrade at Kensington Palace
notices.description:
The works are located within the Boiler Room serving the offices in apartments at Kensington Palace.
The project comprises the replacement of the existing end-of-life atmospheric gas boilers with new high-efficiency condensing boilers, together with the installation of new hot water cylinders, associated pipework, valves and plate heat exchangers. The new heating system shall be designed to facilitate future connection to a heat network, which is currently being investigated through a joint RHPS/HRP feasibility study.
The existing boiler flues, originally designed for atmospheric boilers, shall be surveyed and either replaced or relined as required to suit the new plant. The Contractor shall also assess the adequacy of the existing gas supply and undertake any necessary upgrades, including the replacement of obsolete mechanical gas drop safety valves with modern electrically operated solenoid valves.
The works shall include, but not be limited to:
•Removal and disposal of existing boilers, associated plant and redundant equipment.
•Installation, testing and commissioning of new condensing boilers.
•Installation of new hot water cylinders, plate heat exchangers, pipework, valves and associated ancillaries.
•Survey, replacement and/or relining of existing flues as required.
•Upgrades to the gas supply infrastructure where necessary.
•Removal and replacement of all electrical installations and equipment required to serve the new plant.
•Cleaning, flushing and dosing of the existing heating system to protect both the new plant and retained system components.
•Replacement of all thermostatic radiator valves (TRVs) and lockshield valves.
•Associated builders' work, making good and redecoration of the plant room upon completion of the works.
•Testing, commissioning and provision of all relevant certification, operation and maintenance manuals, and handover documentation.
The completed installation shall provide a significantly improved level of energy efficiency compared with the existing system while maintaining reliable heating and hot water services and enabling future integration with a district heat network.

notices.title: Procurement for Communal Cleaning, Grounds Maintenance and Window Cleaning in Central and East of England (Habinteg)(Split into Lots)
notices.description:
Habinteg Housing Association wishes to appoint one or more Supplier(s) to deliver communal cleaning, window cleaning and grounds maintenance services across its residential schemes in Central and East England.
The services are intended to ensure that communal areas are maintained to an appropriate standard, providing safe, clean and well-maintained environments for residents.
The opportunity has been divided into four Lots, comprising:
- Lot 1: Milton Keynes & Dunstable Grounds Maintenance Services
- Lot 2: Communal Cleaning in Letchworth
- Lot 3: Thetford & Hoveton Grounds Maintenance and Communal Cleaning Services
- Lot 4: Essex & Ipswich Grounds Maintenance, Communal Cleaning and Window Cleaning Services
The successful Supplier(s) will be expected to provide services to all sites within the Lot(s) awarded.
Suppliers may submit a Tender Response for any or all Lots. Each Lot will be evaluated independently, and there is no restriction on the number of Lots that may be awarded to an individual Supplier.
Habinteg welcomes bids from suppliers of all sizes, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and has structured the opportunity into Lots to encourage competition and maximise opportunities for local suppliers.
Suppliers are required to attend a mandatory site visit for the Lot(s) they intend to bid for. Site visit dates, locations and the registration process are detailed within Schedule 1. Suppliers are responsible for ensuring that they attend all mandatory site visits relevant to their Tender Response. Attendance must be registered no later than 12:00 noon on 30th October 2026.
Habinteg has established Lot-specific and site-specific budget caps as detailed within the relevant Schedule 4 - Pricing Schedule. Suppliers must ensure that submitted pricing does not exceed the applicable budget cap(s).
Habinteg is seeking to establish constructive and collaborative relationships with its appointed Supplier(s), working in partnership to deliver high-quality services, achieve value for money and support positive outcomes for residents throughout the Contract Term.
Within the Pricing Schedule, Habinteg has identified the schemes and properties currently requiring service delivery. Should this portfolio require amendment during the Contract Term, including the addition, removal or alteration of schemes, properties or service requirements, this shall be considered the materialisation of a known risk and shall be managed in accordance with the provisions of the Contract.
Please note that Shared Services for Housing Ltd (SSfH) is acting as the managing organisation and procurement lead on behalf of Habinteg Housing Association for this Tendering Procedure.

As public transport comes back under greater public control and significant investment is made in infrastructure, vehicles and customer experience, we have an opportunity to rethink one of the most visible elements of the transport system: the stops, shelters and interchanges for buses and trams.
This is a single stage competitive procedure for initial concept design award, with options to extend the contracts through the following stages:
Stage 1: Concept Design,
Stage 2: Detailed Design, Testing and Commissioning
Stage 3: Manufacture, Install and Supply for key locations
Stage 4: Ongoing supply and install across the network
SYMCA are open for suppliers to approach this commission as a consortium or joint venture project team, to ensure that the appropriate design ambition is achieved.
We are looking for designs that are beautiful but not at the expense of functionality; ambitious but achievable; distinctive but durable and inspiring while remaining safe, inclusive and practical for everyday use.
The consultant shall undertake the role of Principal Designer under the Construction Design Management (CDM) regulations 2015 for the initial design stages of the commission and will then undertake the role of Principal Contractor under the CDM regulations 2015 for the "Build" stage of the commission.

The procurement process aims to appoint a Delivery Partner to deliver and operate a Closed Road Cycle Circuit Facility in the Leckwith area of Cardiff (The Scheme). This contract will be classified as a concession contract under section 8 of the Procurement Act 2023.

Located on the Market Square, Retford Town Hall is well positioned to amplify the offerings of the town, however, the site is currently greatly underutilised, and its facilities require significant modernisation. The Buttermarket is the ground floor premise of the wider Retford Town Hall with its own level and independent access along the Town Hall Yard and direct access to the Market Square. There is ample area (~260m2) to enhance this space to provide a series of catering focused opportunities while also creating an inclusive communal space, designed to host events that appeal across all age groups.
According to a recent market summary of Retford undertaken by CACI, the town boasts a sizable catchment area with a total market potential of £122.1 million. Additionally, Retford enjoys a high catchment market share of 16%, indicating a strong local spend for retailers and food businesses opening in the town centre. The total market potential for catering alone is £30.1 million.
The overall spend remains below the regional average, indicating a need for Retford to build up a critical mass of retail and leisure offer to increase its attractiveness. Annual household spent on catering is £2,060 which is 5% lower than the East Midlands average and spend on alcohol on premises is 10% below the regional average demonstrating there is available spend for these types of offers not currently being realised in Retford.
Mandatory Site Visit
Attendance at a mandatory supervised site visit is a condition of participation in this procurement process.
The site visit will take place at: Buttermarket, Retford Town Hall, DN22 6DE
Site visits will be conducted on 16th November 2026.
Bidders must register in advance to attend the site visit. Instructions for registering and arranging attendance are set out in Section 7.2 of this document.
Only bidders who have successfully registered and attended a site visit in accordance with these instructions will be eligible to submit a tender.
Please note: The Council reserves the right to eliminate bids from the procurement process (without evaluation), that are received from any potential supplier that has not attended a site visit.
Full details of the opportunity and the Council's requirements are set out in the tender documents.
Term
The Council would optimally seek a 5-year lease with a break clause at Year 3 and the opportunity to extend a further 5 years at year 5 (3+2+5 year agreement).
Procurement Procedure
This is a competitive flexible procedure. Initial tenders will be scored based on price quality as out lined in document 1.
Up to the top 3 bidders will then be invited to a presentation stage which will be scored out of 100 (the scoring for which is in appendix 5).
The final tender score will be calculated based on the weightings of the price and quality score from the previous round making up  90% of score and the presentation will form the remaining 10%.

notices.title: UKNNL - Fabrication, Machining, Associated Supplies and Services Open Framework
notices.description:
The framework has the ability to award contracts through restricted quick quotes, open quick quotes, mini competition and direct award. Call-off contracts can be either fixed cost or cost reimbursable. 
Mini-Competition 
Where mini-competition is used, this is to be via the e-tender portal and must include all suppliers on the applicable lot. Each mini competition will be restricted to only one Lot. Should requirements at call-off not have been priced at point of framework creation, mini-competition should be held allowing all suppliers in the applicable Lot to price, accordingly, providing the additional requirement fits within the overall subject matter of the applicable Lot. Mini-competition criteria must not repeat qualification questions. The evaluation criteria must however comprise of the following, with weighting allowances adhered to: 
Evaluation Criteria Range 
•	Pricing 5-90% 
•	Technical 5-90% 
•	Social Value 5-90% 
Mini competitions can be ran using both the Open Procedure and the Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, where the call-off is above threshold. 
The Framework Agreement permits contracts to be awarded by direct award. UKNNL may award a contract directly to a Supplier where this is justified by the requirement for continuity of service, demonstrable value for money, and compliance with applicable procurement legislation.
A direct award can be made to a supplier for the continuation of existing services. This approach is considered appropriate where the supplier has established knowledge, experience, systems integration, and operational capability that are critical to the effective delivery of the services and where a change of supplier would result in disproportionate cost, disruption, delay, or operational risk.
Further justifications for Direct Award can be found below:
•	It secures the uninterrupted continuation of critical services.
•	The requirement consists of substantially similar or repeat services already being delivered by the current supplier.
•	A change of supplier would require significant transition activity, resulting in additional cost, resource burden, loss of operational knowledge, and increased delivery risk.
•	The supplier is already integrated within existing governance, processes, systems, and delivery arrangements.
•	The proposed award represents value for money when considering both contract costs and the costs and risks associated with supplier transition.
•	The award supports efficient service delivery and maximises public benefit.
UKNNL has assessed that awarding the contract to the current supplier represents the most advantageous commercial outcome and is consistent with the Framework terms and/ or the principles set out within Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023 relating to circumstances where supplier continuity, technical knowledge, interoperability, or the procurement of similar services provide a lawful justification for direct award. 
The Procurement Lead shall ensure that the rationale for direct award is fully documented and demonstrates that:
•	The direct award is objectively justified.
•	The decision delivers value for money and public benefit.
•	The risks and costs associated with changing supplier have been considered.
•	The award complies with the Framework Agreement, the Procurement Act 2023, and all applicable governance requirements.
•	Appropriate transparency and approval requirements have been satisfied prior to contract award. 
If there is a pre-existing relationship with any or other suppliers on the Framework which is in the public interest as it offers value for money or a saving in terms of resource and any other compelling commercially and/or value led reason that can be determined to make a Direct Award. 
Additional Direct Award Options - Lot 5 Only
a)	Direct award to the highest ranked supplier 
Admission to the Framework is based on a 50% technical evaluation and 50% commercial evaluation, with Framework Suppliers ranked in descending order according to their combined score. 
For a direct award under the ranking option, the Procurement Lead will approach the highest ranked Framework Supplier on Lot 5 and request a full quotation and indicative delivery programme for the requirement. Social value may be required for contracts delivered under Lot 5, where this is required, suppliers will be required to provide social value commitments within their proposal.
The Procurement Lead may not negotiate the scope of the requirement in a manner that would materially alter the nature of the direct award. Where the highest ranked Framework Supplier is unable to meet the requirement, is unable to deliver within the required timescale, or does not provide a commercially acceptable quotation, the Procurement Lead may progress to the next highest ranked Framework Supplier on Lot 5.
UKNNL is expected to award to the highest ranked Framework Supplier capable of meeting the requirement. However, where there is a demonstrable value-for-money benefit, a pre-existing project relationship, programme continuity requirement, or another compelling commercial justification, the Authority may award to an alternative Framework Supplier, as detailed in 3.4. In such circumstances, the Procurement Lead must ensure that the rationale for the award is appropriately documented and demonstrates the achievement of value for money and public benefit.
b)	Direct award using the desktop calculator
This direct award mechanism enables the Procurement Lead to undertake a weighted evaluation of technical quality and pricing.
The desktop calculator will determine the Most Advantageous Tender by applying a new tender specific weighting to each of the Framework Suppliers’ technical and commercial scores achieved during framework establishment. The supplier with the highest combined technical and commercial score post weighting will be invited to provide a proposal. The desktop calculator must be used to calculate the final ranking. The new revised costing will not be a factor of the evaluation used to determine the highest ranked supplier. The Procurement Lead may determine the relative weighting of Technical and Price, provided that the combined weighting totals 100% and remains within the permitted ranges set out below. Social value may be required for contracts delivered under Lot 5, where this is required, suppliers will be required to provide social value commitments within their proposal.
Following completion of the desktop evaluation, the requirement should be awarded to the highest ranked Framework Supplier. If that supplier is unable to meet the requirement, deliver within the required timescales, or satisfy any mandatory project requirements, the Procurement Lead may progress to the next highest ranked supplier until a suitable supplier is identified.
The business area shall advise on the appropriate balance between Technical and Price having regard to the nature, complexity, and risk associated with the requirement. The values applied must fall within the ranges shown below.
The weighting between Price and Technical will be dependent upon the specifics of each call-off but must be within the range set out below. Evaluation Criteria Range Pricing 5-95% Technical 5-95%.

notices.buyer: The Mayor and Commonalty and Citizens of the City of London
notices.description:
Barbican Renewal Programme - Metalwork Including Feature Stairs
The package covers the design, supply and installation of architectural metalwork and feature stairs across six work areas: the Conservatory (CN), Stair 8 (S8), the Art Gallery Foyers (AF), the Foyers (FY), the Catering Block (CB) and Infrastructure (IN). The items are a mix of new, proprietary and refurbished heritage metalwork, and the Conservatory stairs, balustrades and walkways are the largest part of the package. The scope within each area is summarised below:
•	Conservatory (CN) – feature stairs: Free-standing Helical and Spiral stairs, and the West, East and South ground-bearing stairs, with their balustrades and the helical stair void guarding and gate.
•	Conservatory (CN) – balustrades, gates and handrails: new glazed and planter balustrades to the flytower walkways, viewing platform, landscape and entrance ramp; refurbishment of the Arid House balcony and Level 06 flytower walkway balustrades; guarding to automated doors; gates; and brass handrails to ramps and steps.
•	Conservatory (CN)– walkways and ladders: repairs to the existing access stair, platform and walkway; the duct-protection walkway; the Tower Walkway floor grille; The Ledge access platform; and the Shaft 20 access ladder and extendable pole.
•	Conservatory (CN) – linings, fixtures and louvres: lift architraves, stainless linings, fascias, floor hatches, Theatre Fans louvred doors and screens, the Sculpture Court louvre screen, fin-tube heater brackets fixed to concrete, brass armrests, propagation benches, climber mesh, planters and the Nursery plant shelter; metal planter and lattice soffit repair; and new standalone mechanical louvres and refurbished vent panels fitted into existing openings.
•	Stair 8 (S8): refurbished balustrade with new glass; the Stair 8 ­façade handrail removed, refurbished and refitted with LED lighting; and a perforated deck.
•	Art Gallery Foyers (AF): refurbished mechanical louvres; and, to the Level 03 balconies, a new glazed balustrade and gate and bespoke metal planters.
•	Foyers (FY) : hoop barriers, brass skirting, a goods-lift door, a brass mesh screen, recreated, refurbished and new balustrades, brass handrails, an access slope, foot-pump covers, drink shelves, cycle stands, refurbished louvres, and brass and hose reel cover plates. The brass handrail at the glazing is refurbished by TP4750 and free-issued to TP3300 Glazing and Envelop contractor for refitting.
•	Catering Block (CB): offsite repair and reinstatement of the Level 1 balustrade; a new Level 2 balustrade inside the glazing, demountable for glazing access; a brass hoop barrier; and a terrace planter.
•	Infrastructure (IN): plant fencing and gates, a loading bay gate, plantroom guarding, a fire-rated plant enclosure, ductwork panelling, the Service Road grille, and shaft-top louvre and bird mesh.
Design Responsibility 
The package’s bespoke architectural metalwork and feature stair systems are Contractor Design Portion. The design team specifications set performance requirements and design intent only; the Contractor develops that intent into a complete, buildable design, including structural calculations, fabrication and shop drawings, connection design back to the primary and secondary structure, the Building Regulations approvals that depend on them, and coordination at every interface with adjoining trades. Naming a specific product or finish does not relieve the Contractor of that responsibility.
This includes the full structural design of the Helical, Spiral, West, East and South feature stairs; structural adequacy and loading design for all balustrades, guarding, working platforms and walkways, including permanent fall-restraint systems and their certification; and a condition-survey-led repair method and specification for every refurbishment item.

Ironwork

Street furniture
